editorial:
If you grew up watching the Smurfs or have kids who love colorful adventures, this fully animated reboot is a fun ride. The story follows Smurfette, who feels out of place because she is the only girl in her village. When she finds a mysterious map, she and her friends Brainy, Clumsy, and Hefty sneak into the Forbidden Forest to find a hidden Smurf village. Along the way, they face wild creatures, tricky paths, and the evil wizard Gargamel, who wants to capture every Smurf. The animation is bright and lively, and the forest scenes feel like a colorful playground full of surprises. It is a simple, feel-good adventure that keeps things moving without getting too heavy.

The voice cast does a solid job, especially Demi Lovato as Smurfette, who gives the character real heart. The pacing is quick, so younger viewers will not get bored, and there are plenty of silly jokes for adults too. On the downside, the story is pretty predictable, and some characters feel a bit one-note. Still, if you want a cozy family movie night, this one delivers. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Smurfette and her friends discover the lost village, which is home to female Smurfs. Gargamel attacks and tries to capture them all, but Smurfette sacrifices herself to save her friends. The other Smurfs use their magic to bring her back to life, and she finally feels like she truly belongs. The two villages unite, and everyone celebrates together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves colorful family adventures and lighthearted animated movies.
